Package graphics

Class SimpleCanvas

java.lang.Object
graphics.SimpleCanvas
public class SimpleCanvas extends Object
A SimpleCanvas represents a window on the screen that can be drawn on.

    • drawArc

      public void drawArc(int centerX, int centerY, int radius, int startAngle, int arcAngle)
      Draws an arc (a portion of an oval's outline) centered at (centerX, centerY) with the specified radius. The arc begins at startAngle and extends for arcAngle degrees. Angles are in degrees, with 0 at the 3 o'clock position, increasing counterclockwise.
      Parameters:
      centerX - the x-coordinate of the center of the arc
      centerY - the y-coordinate of the center of the arc
      radius - the radius of the arc, in pixels
      startAngle - the angle at which the arc begins, in degrees
      arcAngle - how far the arc extends, in degrees; positive sweeps counterclockwise

    • drawImageRotated

      public void drawImageRotated(int centerX, int centerY, String filename, int degrees)
      Draws the specified image on the canvas, rotated by the given number of degrees. Note: unlike drawImage, (centerX, centerY) specifies the CENTER of the image, not the top left corner. The image rotates in place around this center point. Positive degrees rotate clockwise. The filename can be a file path, URL, or classpath resource.
      Parameters:
      centerX - the x-coordinate of the center of the image
      centerY - the y-coordinate of the center of the image
      filename - the file path, URL, or classpath resource of the image
      degrees - how far to rotate the image, in degrees; positive rotates clockwise

    • preloadSound

      public void preloadSound(String filename)
      Preloads the specified WAV file into an internal cache so that the first call to playSound() on that file plays without delay. Calling this method is optional: playSound() will preload automatically on first use, but doing so during an animation loop can cause a visible hitch.

      This method is synchronous and may take noticeable time to open and decode the file. Call preloadSound() during program setup, before your animation loop begins -- not from inside the loop itself.

      Subsequent calls with the same filename are no-ops. The filename can be a file path, URL, or classpath resource.

      Parameters:
      filename - the file path, URL, or classpath resource of the WAV file

    • fixSounds

      public void fixSounds()
      Starts a silent audio clip looping in the background to keep the operating system's audio driver active. On some systems (notably macOS), the OS can put the audio driver to sleep, causing a noticeable delay the next time a sound is played. Calling fixSounds() prevents that delay.

      This fix is optional and not needed on every system. Call it once near the start of your program if you notice latency when playing sounds. Subsequent calls are no-ops.

    • playSound

      public void playSound(String filename)
      Plays the specified WAV file once. Playback is non-blocking (the method returns immediately). If the file has not been preloaded, it is loaded on first call -- this can cause a brief delay, so consider calling preloadSound() during setup.

      Rapidly re-triggering the same sound restarts it from the beginning rather than overlapping playback.

      Parameters:
      filename - the file path, URL, or classpath resource of the WAV file

    • loopSound

      public void loopSound(String filename)
      Loops the specified WAV file continuously until stopSound() is called or another loopSound() call replaces it. Playback is non-blocking.
      Parameters:
      filename - the file path, URL, or classpath resource of the WAV file

    • stopSound

      public void stopSound()
      Stops the currently looping sound, if any.

    • update

      public void update()
      If any drawing operations have taken place, update() actually draws them to the canvas. Shapes are not normally drawn instantaneously; instead, they are not drawn until this method is called. Therefore, this method can be used to have a number of new shapes all appear simultaneously on the screen.
